Published - October 21, 2026 01:21 pm IST - Saint Petersburg
Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev greets U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff upon his arrival at Pulkovo Airport in Saint Petersburg, Russia, October 21, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters
Washington's envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in Saint Petersburg early Wednesday (October 21, 2026) to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin following what U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio described as "positive" talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine.
The trip by President Donald Trump's special envoy is part of efforts to draw a line under a bitter feud between him and Mr. Zelenskyy over the war with Russia.
After talks with Mr. Witkoff in Oslo, Mr. Zelenskyy thanked Washington on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) for the resumption of U.S. intelligence sharing on Russian strikes.
The positive tone followed days of friction between Kyiv and Washington after Mr. Trump struck a diesel-supply deal with Mr. Putin and called for Mr. Zelensky to be replaced after Ukraine refused to stop hitting Russian oil refineries.
"We are thankful that intelligence works," Mr. Zelensky told reporters in Oslo, describing the early warnings as "very, very important for our people, for children, adults, civilians" when ballistic missiles were about to strike.
Mr. Rubio said during a visit to India that Mr. Witkoff would next head to Russia after the "positive" talks with Mr. Zelensky
"He'll now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to Saint Petersburg and share them with the Russian side — and let's see if we can make some progress," Mr. Rubio said.
Mr. Witkoff's planned meeting with Mr. Putin on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) would include Mr. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner participating virtually, a U.S. official told AFP .
Mr. Trump's envoy was met at Pulkovo Airport in Saint Petersburg by the Kremlin's adviser for international economic cooperation, Kirill Dmitriev, according to news agencies.
Mr. Trump said on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) that he had asked Putin to release Stephen Hubbard, an American taken captive by Russian forces years earlier in Ukraine, though it was not clear if the request would be raised in Wednesday's (October 21, 2026) talks.
"I've been talking to him at length. I've asked him to release him. Let's see what happens," Mr. Trump told journalists in Washington.
Mr. Trump has also been keeping up the pressure on Ukraine, saying at the White House that he wanted Mr. Zelenskyy to "make a deal" with Russia, which is ramping up its strikes as a bitter winter looms.
Mr. Trump, who called on Mr. Zelenskyy to resign last week, also criticised the Ukrainian president for not accepting terms he said he had offered during an infamous televised row in the Oval Office in February 2025.
Ukraine reacted with dismay after Mr. Trump also waived sanctions against Russia's war machine.
The feud spiralled as Mr. Zelenskyy accused Mr. Trump of weakness, and then alleged that the United States was deliberately withholding vital intelligence and delaying the delivery of interceptor missiles.
Ukraine has also reported a reduction in speeds on Starshield, the U.S. military satellite system it uses for battlefield communications and strikes on Russian-occupied territory.
Mr. Trump has denied ordering a reduction in speeds on Starshield after Elon Musk — whose company SpaceX developed it — said the order could only have come from the White House.
Mr. Rubio said on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) that Washington had no prior knowledge of the slowdown of the SpaceX satellite communications.
"The President has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr. Musk," Mr. Rubio said in Mumbai.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) that it was indeed Mr. Musk who ordered the slowdown in the military-grade version of Starlink.
Mr. Witkoff's meetings follow furious diplomatic efforts in Washington, Kyiv and Western capitals to calm the row.
Mr. Zelenskyy told U.S. senators on Monday (October 19, 2026) that "the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles" already paid for by European countries, while the shipment was waiting for U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's signature.
Several European countries were ready to transfer Patriot interceptor missiles from their own stockpiles but were awaiting U.S. approval, he said.
Mr. Trump, whose Republican Party faces tough midterm elections as fuel prices soar, has accused Mr. Zelenskyy of a lack of effort to resolve the conflict.
He said he was ready to meet Mr. Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in China next month to discuss denuclearisation, adding that talks could also cover the Ukraine war — sparking fears in Kyiv that it was being sidelined.
Mr. Zelensky insisted on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) that Kyiv needed to be represented at any meeting regarding Ukraine's future.
"If there are issues about Ukraine, our future, it can be acceptable only when we are at the table of negotiations," he said.
